description:
Status page transparency upgrades is a cross-functional reliability/comms project within Redwood Inference’s Reliability Program. The goal is to make customer-facing incident communication more accurate, timely, and actionable by (1) increasing status page component granularity, (2) standardizing incident communication templates (initial/identified/monitoring/resolved) and update cadence guidance, and (3) publishing consistent post-incident summaries that align with internal postmortems while respecting security/privacy constraints.

Why now: Redwood’s platform spans Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments across multiple regions. As usage has grown (and with more enterprise SLAs), customers increasingly rely on the public status page to understand partial degradations (e.g., streaming-only errors, specific model families, region-specific capacity constraints) and to make routing/fallback decisions.

Scope:
- Component granularity: Define a customer-comprehensible taxonomy (e.g., API Gateway, Streaming, Embeddings, Rerank, Console, Dedicated Control Plane, Private Control Plane, Region-specific Serving) and map internal services/alerts to public components.
- Incident comms templates: Provide copy-ready templates and guidance for what to say at each phase, including uncertainty language, mitigation/workaround statements, and next update timing.
- Post-incident summaries: A lightweight, customer-facing summary format derived from internal postmortems (impact, timeline, root cause category, mitigations, prevention) with a defined SLA (e.g., within 3 business days for Sev1/Sev0).
- Tooling: Updates to incident-bot / internal workflows to reduce manual work and ensure the status page stays in sync with incident state transitions.

Non-goals:
- Changing the underlying incident process fundamentals (roles, severity definitions) beyond what’s needed to support external comms.
- Publishing sensitive details (customer names, exploit details, provider contractual constraints).

Stakeholders:
- Engineering/SRE: Sean Gallagher (Dir SRE), Rafael Mendes (SRE Mgr), Miles Thornton, Tomáš Novák, Aisha Bello, Christine Wong.
- Product (Console & Rollouts): Marissa Cole (Dir), Paula Mendes (Sr PM).
- Support/CS and GTM: support leads and AEs/CSMs for enterprise expectations; Security/Compliance consulted on disclosure boundaries.

Phases & rough timeline (6–8 weeks):
1) Discovery (week 1–2): audit past incidents/support tickets; define taxonomy and mapping; agree disclosure guidelines.
2) Design (week 2–3): comms templates + post-incident summary format; automation approach (incident-bot → status updates).
3) Implementation (week 3–6): status page component changes; bot/workflow changes; documentation updates.
4) Rollout (week 6–8): pilot on one region/service group; train oncall; announce externally; measure outcomes (fewer support escalations, improved CSAT, reduced time-to-first-update, reduced “what’s impacted?” follow-ups).

Key deliverables:
- Confluence: published taxonomy, templates, and procedures; runbook updates.
- Linear: tracked workstream with acceptance criteria.
- GitHub: PRs for incident-bot changes, metrics, status page config, docs.
- Slack: operational coordination threads and incident comms reviews.
- Drive: drafts/decks and working notes.
- Support/CRM: customer-facing expectations captured via Jira/Gmail/HubSpot and a few enterprise security-review transcripts (Fireflies).
